== Biography ==
Robert was born about 1728. He is the son of [[Glasgow-1077|John Glasgow]] and [[Ferguson-15168|Agnes Ferguson]]. 



=== '''Robert Glasgow (b. 1728)''' ===

'''Robert Glasgow''' (born '''1728''') was a Scottish estate manager and businessman, notable for serving as '''factor''' for the '''Viscount of Garnock'''. His career included managing the '''Kilbirnie and Glengarnock estates''' in Ayrshire, and he was involved in key financial and legal matters concerning these properties.

=== Early Life and Family ===

Robert Glasgow was born in '''1728''', the son of '''John Glasgow MA''', a prominent figure in Glasgow, and '''Agnes Ferguson'''. His father, John, held significant civic roles, including serving as Provost of Glasgow. Robert’s uncle, also named '''Robert Glasgow''', was a noted surgeon and Chamberlain of the Garnock estate, who married '''Margaret Allan''' in 1736. The Glasgow family was well connected in both the civic and landed communities of Ayrshire and beyond.

=== Career ===

Following in the footsteps of his family’s tradition of public service and estate management, Robert became the '''factor for the Viscount of Garnock''', responsible for overseeing the '''Kilbirnie''' and '''Glengarnock estates'''. His work as factor included managing financial affairs, estate upkeep, and tenant relations. One notable episode involved a dispute over documents related to the '''Smith family''' of Todhill, where Robert's role as '''Smith's maternal grandfather''' placed him at the center of legal discussions about estate ownership.

===Personal Life ===

Robert Glasgow remained closely tied to his family’s long-standing involvement in estate management and civic affairs. Though he did not gain as much wealth or international recognition as some of his relatives, his work as a factor for Lord Garnock solidified his place in the history of estate management in Ayrshire.

=== Legacy ===

Robert Glasgow's legacy is tied to his management of the Garnock estates and his familial connections to influential civic figures in Ayrshire. His careful stewardship of the estates and involvement in important legal matters demonstrate his role in maintaining the financial health and governance of the region during the mid-18th century.
